subtopics.title: Population Growth and the Demographic Cycle

questions.question: Population size changes through:
options: NATURAL GROWTH (births minus deaths) and MIGRATION (arrivals minus departures)

questions.question: 25 births and 10 deaths per thousand gives a natural growth rate of:
options: 15 per thousand — one comma five percent a year

questions.question: Stage two (early expanding) of the demographic cycle features:
options: Death rates FALLING (water, vaccines, food) while birth rates stay high — the gap driving rapid growth
Falling birth rates with rising deaths

questions.question: Birth rates fall in stage three because of:
options: Urbanisation, education — especially of women — family planning, and children shifting from farm labour to school costs

questions.question: The labour force consists of:
options: Working-age people who are EMPLOYED plus those unemployed by the strict definition — without work, available, and actively seeking

questions.question: Discouraged work-seekers are:
options: Wanting work but no longer searching — excluded by the strict definition, counted back by the EXPANDED definition

questions.question: The unemployment rate divides the unemployed by:
options: The LABOUR FORCE — dividing by the wrong bowl is the classic error

questions.question: South Africa's labour force profile shows:
options: An old labour force with low youth unemployment
A YOUNG labour force with youth unemployment far above the national rate, jobs clustered in metropolitan cores, and participation suppressed by discouragement

subtopics.title: The Demand and Supply for Labour

questions.question: Labour demand is a DERIVED demand because:
options: Firms want workers for the OUTPUT they produce — demand for builders derives from demand for buildings

questions.question: In the labour market, the counter turns around:
options: HOUSEHOLDS supply labour, FIRMS demand it, and the WAGE is its price

questions.question: The labour demand curve slopes downward because at higher wages:
options: Firms hire fewer workers, substitute machines, or produce less

questions.question: The SKILLS MISMATCH means:
options: The education pipeline produces too few of what firms seek while millions offer what firms need less of — the structural heart of SA unemployment

questions.question: "Definitions before numbers" means:
options: Quote WHICH definition a figure uses — strict against expanded can differ by millions — before interpreting it

questions.question: Youth unemployment divides:
options: Young unemployed by the whole population
Young unemployed by the YOUNG labour force
All unemployed by the youth population

questions.question: "Structure over headline" warns that:
options: One national rate hides concentrations — among the young, the unskilled and particular provinces — where scenario questions live

questions.question: A comment that ANALYSES rather than describes:
options: Connects the number to its MECHANISM — through demand, supply, skills or geography

questions.question: The street's population change equals:
options: Births minus funerals, plus who moved in minus who moved away — natural growth plus migration

questions.question: "The clinic arrived and the street boomed" describes:
options: The second season — funerals growing rare while cradles stayed full

questions.question: The sentence explaining the whole term is:
options: Every year a big new class finishes school and arrives at the gate looking for work — against the number of gates that open

questions.question: Uncle S'bu — not working, applying at sites, phoning about vacancies — is:
options: On the team, benched but warming up: officially UNEMPLOYED by the strict definition

questions.question: The matric sister at school full-time is:
options: NOT in the labour force — learners don't count on the team sheet

questions.question: Cousin Jabu — wants work, stopped searching — is:
options: Off the strict team sheet but counted by the EXPANDED definition — the gap between the counts is thousands of real Jabus

questions.question: Jabu's quiet exit shows up statistically in:
options: PARTICIPATION falling — discouragement hides there, not in the strict unemployment rate

subtopics.title: The Wage Is a Price at a Gate

questions.question: In the labour market the sellers and buyers are:
options: FAMILIES selling hours and skills; FIRMS buying them — the wage as the meeting price
Firms selling jobs; families buying them

questions.question: "No orders, no shifts" is the street version of:
options: DERIVED demand — the demand for labour is borrowed from the demand for goods

questions.question: The engineers' gate and the general-labour gate show:
options: Wages set by law at both gates
The market split by SKILL — short queue and strong wages at one, long queue and pressed wages at the other

questions.question: "A certificate is a ticket" means:
options: Training moves a worker from the crowded gate to the short one — the ladder across the skills mismatch
